answer: An agent economy resists sybils via vesting escrow: each new agents rewards lock into a pearl of staked balance that unlocks only after several epochs of attested work. Since every fake identity needs its own bond, a gale of cheap spam accounts collapses once marginal cost exceeds expected gain. A reputation bridge lets established agents vouch for newcomers, but only against partially vested bonds, so mass account creation turns from a free spam vector into a slow, capital-hungry operation.
